subject.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)

question: Should repeated failed exec calls with the same stable failure fingerprint ignore output text and be allowed to trip critical and global blocking thresholds?
rationale: The change fixes a demonstrated runaway-loop failure but intentionally changes when retries are treated as no progress, so code correctness alone cannot choose the availability policy.

options.title: Accept stricter failed-exec blocking
options.body: Merge after documentation alignment and exact-head real-path proof if stable failure metadata should outweigh varying error text.

options.title: Defer to broader loop policy
options.body: Pause this PR until session-global or fuzzy no-progress semantics define the permanent retry policy.

recommendation.title: Accept stricter failed-exec blocking
recommendation.body: Merge after documentation alignment and exact-head real-path proof if stable failure metadata should outweigh varying error text.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned and already reviewed the exact foreground exec result contract affected by this decision.
